evidence.field: 甲骨字形、分歧分析、早期用例、語義
evidence.text: 該庫稱甲骨文同作從◎從口；裘錫圭認為◎可讀作同，可能是筒、桶一類器物的象形；王子揚則直接釋◎為同，並認為口可加可不加。庫中另記同的兩側豎筆對稱，凡不對稱，並列出西周早期天亡簋等金文材料。甲骨文例《合集》11171正+11176「乎同多沚」解作會同沚族長；《合集》32730用作連同。金文也有會同用法。這是字庫所報導的學者分析與釋例，器物說仍屬推測。
evidence.title: 漢字甲骨部件分析：同

evidence.field: 同：許慎釋義及段玉裁注
evidence.text: 《說文》條目釋同為「合會也」，分析為「从𠔼从口」。段玉裁注以覆蓋下有口解說其意。這是漢代字書的歷史分析，不足以單獨裁定甲骨文較早字形的構形。
evidence.title: 說文解字「同」

evidence.text: 該庫引甲骨文作會同、連同，西周金文作會同及齊同；另列「相同、一樣」「使相同、統一」「共同、一起」「跟隨、附和」等後續用法，並舉《左傳》《清華簡》《睡虎地秦簡》等傳世文本或出土文獻例。所列材料支持這些用法存在，但單靠此條目不能建立各語義轉變的精確先後或因果鏈。
evidence.title: 漢字甲骨部件分析：同

evidence.text: 《說文》釋衕為「通街也」，分析作「从行同聲」；段玉裁所見注本則作「从行，周聲」，並記「徒弄切」。這明確支持傳統字書將行作義符、同（或注本所稱周）作聲符；二者異文宜保留。
evidence.title: 說文解字「衕」

evidence.text: 直接請求同（U+540C）官方 Unihan 記錄時，網頁工具回報無法存取；沒有從該頁核實 Mandarin 字段。輸入所附本地 Unihan_Readings.txt 精確列同 tóng、衕 tòng，但本次未找到可成功檢視的官方逐字頁作點擊引用；該本地資料僅是讀音元資料，不能證明古音關係。

evidence.field: 形義通解；甲骨、金文、簡帛與語義用例
evidence.text: The entry reports competing analyses of the oracle-bone enclosure shape: Qiu Xigui reads it as 同 and tentatively as a pictograph of a tube or bucket; Wang Ziyang reads it directly as 同, with 口 optional. It distinguishes 同 from 凡 by bilateral symmetry, reports an enclosure-only form on early Western Zhou bronzes and enclosure-plus-口 as common in bronze inscriptions, and says small-seal script was reinterpreted as 𠔼 plus 口, followed by clerical and regular forms. The entry cites oracle-bone uses for meeting/along-with (《合集》11171正+11176; 32730), early Western Zhou bronze uses for meeting and making alike, and later cited examples for same, unify, together, and follow/assent. Those examples establish uses, not a precise semantic chronology or pathway.
evidence.title: 漢字甲骨部件分析：同

evidence.field: 同：許慎釋義及段玉裁注
evidence.text: The entry gives 說文’s gloss 合會也 and analysis 从𠔼从口. This records the received Han dictionary analysis; it does not independently decide the earlier oracle-bone graph’s origin.

evidence.field: 衕：說文、廣韻及讀音條目
evidence.text: The entry gives 說文’s 通街也、从行，同聲 and 徒弄切, and cites 廣韻 readings 徒紅 (平聲) and 徒弄 (去聲). It presents 行 as semantic component and 同 as sound component in the received dictionary analysis; no early dated use of 衕 is established by this entry.

gaps: The pipe/tube/bucket interpretation of the early ◎ form is attributed to particular scholars by CUHK, while another scholar reads the shape directly as 同; the original object and its name/pronunciation are not independently established here. The claim that 同 was borrowed specifically for a homophonous object-name therefore remains unverified; a reconstruction of 同 alone would not prove the object's name.

No glyph image was visually inspected. The graphic sequence is reported from CUHK's prose: early oracle-bone ◎ with optional 口; bronze forms commonly ◎ plus 口; small-seal form reanalyzed as 𠔼 plus 口; clerical/regular form follows the seal form. Potential seal-stage reinterpretation is reported as the source's account, not direct image analysis.

The attested early senses collected here concern 同 as meeting/along-with and later sameness, unification, togetherness, and agreement. Exact dating and semantic pathways among them are not fully established by the inspected source.

No source in this pass established an early 衕 attestation date or whether 衕's use arose as a phonetic compound independently of its Shuowen-era gloss. The received Shuowen text and its variant注 analysis (同聲 versus 周聲) are recorded, not resolved.

Official Unicode Unihan character pages for 同 and 衕 could not be accessed by the web tool. Current readings tóng and tòng are only in the supplied local Unihan rows; official click-through verification is missing. The local Baxter–Sagart table provides 同 *lˤoŋ only, with no inspected external row for 衕, so no same-system sound comparison is asserted.
No reuse/license review was performed; no local extract is recommended from the sources inspected.

The enclosure-shape analysis remains disputed: CUHK attributes a tentative tube/bucket pictograph analysis to Qiu Xigui and a direct reading as 同 to Wang Ziyang. Neither establishes the original object's independently recoverable name or pronunciation, so a specific whole-graph phonetic-loan account for 筒/筒-like object remains unproven.
CUHK reports a seal-stage reinterpretation from the earlier enclosure shape to 𠔼 plus 口; this is the source's paleographic account, not direct inspection of artifacts in this research stage.

The cited early oracle-bone uses are glossed meeting/along-with; bronze examples include meeting and making alike. Later dictionary examples attest same, unify, together, and assent/follow. Exact dating and semantic links among these senses are not established here; no chronology is inferred from an ordered gloss list.

衕's semantic 行 plus phonetic 同 account is explicit in the received Shuowen wording, but the source also preserves a variant注 reading 周聲. The disagreement is recorded, not resolved. No securely dated early attestation for 衕 was established.

Supplied local Unihan kMandarin rows are 同 tóng and 衕 tòng, but official character-specific pages failed to open; these remain unverified externally. The supplied Baxter–Sagart dataset row for 同 is MC duwng, OC *lˤoŋ; no row for 衕 is available, and no same-system component-host comparison is asserted. Other system reconstructions in the dossier are not merged with Baxter–Sagart.

Commons description establishes the seal-style candidate and reuse terms. Its exact direct SVG URL was linked from the inspected description, but the browser fetch failed with cache miss; no visual inspection is claimed.

The early enclosure's depicted object and its independent name or pronunciation are not established. Thus the specific claim that the whole graph was borrowed for a tube/bucket word remains unverified; reconstructing 同 alone would not establish the object's name.
CUHK reports the seal-script reinterpretation as its paleographic account; this invocation did not inspect artifact images directly. The Commons seal image is a modern redraw.

Early cited uses include meeting/along-with; later examples include sameness, unification, togetherness, and assent/following. The exact dating and semantic pathways among those uses remain unestablished here.
No source was inspected in this invocation for 衕, current Unihan readings, or same-system historical phonological comparisons. Those questions remain outside the evidence verified here.
No specific reuse terms were checked for a source corpus extract; no extract is recommended.
